name: factor_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Academic factor investing (value + momentum) works at monthly frequencies but is under-explored intraday. Stocks that are relatively cheap (low P/E within sector) AND showing strong intraday momentum (top quartile of 60-min returns) tend to outperform in the subsequent 30-60 minutes. The inefficiency exists because institutional factor investors operate on daily+ horizons, and retail intraday traders ignore fundamental factors. The value tilt prevents chasing expensive momentum stocks that are prone to sharp reversals, while momentum prevents value traps that keep falling.
universe: NIFTY 100 constituents grouped by GICS sector
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹50 Cr; sector must have >= 5 members for cross-sectional ranking

indicators.name: Value_Rank
indicators.params: percentile_rank(PE_ratio, sector_peers) — lower PE = higher value rank

long.confirmation: ROC(close, 5) > 0 (short-term momentum still positive over last 5 bars)

exit.trailing_stop: After 30 bps profit, trail at 20 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Composite_Score drops below 0.50 (for longs) or rises above 0.50 (for shorts)

filters.time_filter: No entries before 10:15 (need 60 bars for momentum calc) or after 15:00
filters.volume_filter: Stock volume in last 60 bars > 50th percentile of its 20-day avg
filters.trend_filter: Sector index for the stock must not be down > 2% from previous close
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day and for 2 days after
other_filters: Sector must have at least 5 liquid members for meaningful cross-sectional ranking

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — combining fundamental (value) with technical (momentum) factors at intraday frequency is uncommon; academic-to-practical gap protects edge

weaknesses: PE ratio is a daily/quarterly metric — using it for intraday decisions mixes time horizons awkwardly; PE does not change intraday, so value rank is static for the session
Cross-sectional ranking requires real-time computation across sector peers, adding latency; if a sector has only 5-6 liquid names, ranks are noisy
60-bar momentum lookback delays signals — by the time a stock reaches top quintile momentum, the move may be 50-70% complete, limiting remaining upside
prior_art: Fama-French factor models; Asness et al. (2013) 'Value and Momentum Everywhere'; Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) momentum; intraday factor application is novel but built on established theory
notes: The 0.4/0.6 value/momentum weighting favors momentum because intraday price dynamics matter more than static fundamental factors. Consider adding a quality factor (ROE rank) as a third component.
